findings.detail: Independent reproduction before the change confirmed that pinned Torch 2.8.0+cpu exposes torch.__version__ as a TorchVersion subclass rather than an exact str. The strict canonical JSON validator rejected the original runtime identity with invalid_json: value.torch is not finite JSON. The prospective freeze revealed this before declaration publication; the freeze path constructs no physical host or policy model.

The conversion preserves the exact version text 2.8.0+cpu while providing the plain JSON scalar required by the unchanged serializer. NumPy already supplies a plain string. Runtime equality, pinned-version checks, source and review binding, host identity, budgets, training configuration, policy semantics and qualification remain unchanged.

The new test uses the installed runtime identity rather than a mocked string, publishes through the immutable production JSON writer and reads through the strict production reader. It verifies the full reconstructed identity and canonical hash and checks the restored Torch field's exact type and value. All 20 screen tests pass in the pinned environment.

A separate standard-library enumeration and byte-hash reconstruction confirms 182 files at the new aggregate hash. Comparing every inventoried file with the published parent identifies exactly the two declared source/test changes; the remaining 180 source inventory entries retain their original bytes. The original policy review is unchanged. This supplement accepts the new complete source inventory subject to its own clean source publication and required hosted checks.
